Every input here starts as NetCDF files of a Copernicus Marine in situ
product. [ctddump](https://aiqc-hub.github.io/ctddump/) converts them to one
flat table per product, then cleans and de-duplicates it in four steps.
[seastamp](https://aiqc-hub.github.io/seastamp/) adds the distance to the
coast and the sea floor depth, and nrtqclib runs its tests on the result. This
page follows the profiles through those steps, from the reports ctddump
writes as it goes. A full ctddump report for one product is
[published as an example](https://aiqc-hub.github.io/ctddump-report-example/nrt_ar_ar.html).

::: {.callout-note}
## CORA is not another NRT product

CORA is a reprocessed collection: its profiles have been through quality
control again after the fact, with automated tests and checks by
operators, so its flags are closer to delayed mode than to NRT. It is converted
here the same way as the NRT products, so its steps, duplicates and overlap
sit beside theirs. The rest of the site files every CORA profile as delayed
mode, even though its files declare them real time (R) wherever they
declare a mode at all.
:::

```{ojs}
//| output: false
app = import(new URL("assets/js/app.js", document.baseURI).href)
meta = app.loadAnalyses()
name = (id) => app.datasetName(meta, id)
byDataset = (a, b) => app.datasetOrder(meta, a.dataset_id) - app.datasetOrder(meta, b.dataset_id)
table = app.analysisTable
```

```{ojs}
meta === null ? app.analysesMissing() : html``
```

## The steps

ctddump drops, in this order: profiles whose time or position its source
flags as bad, profiles with no value in any variable, profiles outside the
product's region (the global product covers the world, and only its part
of the region is kept), and duplicate profiles, which have
[a section of their own](#duplicates-within-a-product). What is left after
the last step is what nrtqclib checked: seastamp adds columns, not rows, and
the analyses check that each nrtqclib output holds exactly the profiles and
observations ctddump kept.

```{ojs}
steps = meta ? app.loadAnalysisTable("conversion_steps") : null
stepNames = steps ? [...new Map(steps.map((r) => [r.step, r.step_label]))] : []
stepRows = steps
  ? app.widen(steps, { index: ["dataset_id"], column: "step", value: "n_profiles" })
      .sort(byDataset)
      .map((row) => ({ ...row, key: row.dataset_id, name: name(row.dataset_id) }))
  : []
meta ? app.analysisFigure(
  "conversion_steps",
  "Profiles left after each ctddump step, as a share of the profiles converted. The last point is what nrtqclib checked.",
  "Line chart of the share of profiles kept after each step, one panel per region."
) : html``
```

```{ojs}
stepHeadings = ({
  convert: "Converted", dropqc: "After QC", dropna: "After all missing",
  filter: "In region", dedup: "Without duplicates"
})
meta ? table(stepRows, [
  { key: "name", label: "Product", align: "left", format: (v) => v },
  ...stepNames.map(([key, label]) => ({ key, label: stepHeadings[key] ?? label, title: label })),
  { key: "kept", label: "Kept", format: (_, row) => app.formatShare(row[stepNames.at(-1)?.[0]], row.convert) }
]) : html``
```

## The source files

How many files each product has, how many carry each variable ctddump reads,
and the data mode their global attributes declare. `M` (mixed) means the
levels of a file are in different modes: ctddump then needs a data mode per
level to know which, and writes an empty mode when the file has none.

```{ojs}
files = meta ? app.loadAnalysisTable("conversion_files") : null
fileModes = meta ? app.loadAnalysisTable("conversion_file_data_mode") : null
fileRows = files
  ? app.widen(files, { index: ["dataset_id", "n_files"], column: "item", value: "n_with" })
      .map((row) => {
        const modes = (fileModes ?? []).filter((m) => m.dataset_id === row.dataset_id);
        const count = (mode) => modes.filter((m) => (m.data_mode ?? "") === mode).reduce((s, m) => s + m.n_files, 0);
        return { ...row, key: row.dataset_id, name: name(row.dataset_id),
                 R: count("R"), D: count("D"), M: count("M"), none: count("") };
      })
      .sort(byDataset)
  : []
meta ? table(fileRows, [
  { key: "name", label: "Product", align: "left", format: (v) => v },
  { key: "n_files", label: "Files" },
  ...["temp", "psal", "pres", "deph", "time_qc", "position_qc"].map((item) => ({
    key: item, label: `With ${item.toUpperCase()}`,
    format: (v, row) => app.formatShare(v, row.n_files)
  })),
  { key: "R", label: "Mode R" },
  { key: "D", label: "Mode D" },
  { key: "M", label: "Mode M" },
  { key: "none", label: "No mode" }
]) : html``
```

## Data modes

The data mode of every temperature observation, at the two ends of the
pipeline: as converted (step 1) and as kept (after step 5, the profiles
nrtqclib checked). A profile with a delayed mode observation is compared
separately on the rest of the site, because its input flags are likely to be
an operator's: see [NRT and delayed mode](analyses-data-mode.qmd). CORA is
filed there whole whatever its data mode says, because CORA's flags come
from its own reprocessing.

```{ojs}
meta ? app.analysisFigure(
  "conversion_data_mode",
  "Temperature observations by data mode, as converted (step 1) and as kept (after step 5). No data mode: the file gives none for the observation.",
  "Stacked bars of the data mode share per product, before and after cleaning."
) : html``
```

**No data mode.** ctddump gives every observation of every variable a data
mode: R (real time), A (adjusted in real time) or D (delayed mode). It takes
it from the file's data mode per level (such as `TEMP_DM`), failing that from
the variable's `data_mode` attribute, and for CORA from the data mode of the
profile. When none of those says R, A or D, the observation has no data
mode. Here that happens in two ways:

- **At a level with no value.** The per level data mode is empty wherever the
  variable itself is, so a missing value comes with a missing data mode. This
  is nearly all of what the NRT products show, and the cleaning steps remove
  most of it with the empty levels.
- **In files that give none.** Some Baltic CORA files have no data mode at
  all, and every observation in them has none.

The first kind says nothing about the profile, so the groups on the rest of
the site count a missing data mode only where the variable has a value. The
table gives the counts the shares above hide.

```{ojs}
modeCounts = meta ? app.loadAnalysisTable("conversion_data_mode") : null
noModeRows = modeCounts
  ? app.widen(
      modeCounts.filter((r) => r.variable === "temp"),
      { index: ["dataset_id"], column: "step", value: "n_obs", name: (s) => s }
    ).map((row) => {
      const of = (step, empty) => modeCounts
        .filter((r) => r.dataset_id === row.dataset_id && r.variable === "temp" && r.step === step && (((r.data_mode ?? "") === "") === empty))
        .reduce((sum, r) => sum + r.n_obs, 0);
      return {
        key: row.dataset_id, dataset_id: row.dataset_id,
        convert_none: of("convert", true), convert_all: row.convert,
        dedup_none: of("dedup", true), dedup_all: row.dedup
      };
    }).sort(byDataset)
  : []
meta ? table(noModeRows, [
  { key: "dataset_id", label: "Product", align: "left", format: name },
  { key: "convert_none", label: "No data mode, converted" },
  { key: "convert_share", label: "Share", format: (_, r) => app.formatShare(r.convert_none, r.convert_all) },
  { key: "dedup_none", label: "No data mode, kept" },
  { key: "dedup_share", label: "Share", format: (_, r) => app.formatShare(r.dedup_none, r.dedup_all) }
]) : html``
```

## Duplicates within a product

Step 5 treats two profiles of one product as duplicates when they were
taken on the same date at the same position, rounded to three decimals of a
degree (about 100 m or less). The platform code is not part of the match, so
a group of duplicates is one of three kinds:

- **Within one platform:** every profile of the group carries the same
  platform code. One platform reported the same cast more than once.
- **Across platforms:** every profile carries a different platform code.
  The same cast reached the product under different names, once each.
- **Both:** the group spans two or more platform codes, and at least one of
  them reports the cast more than once. The cast was repeated and renamed.

Of each group ctddump keeps the profile with the most observations and
removes the rest, so a group of two loses one profile.

```{ojs}
meta ? app.analysisFigure(
  "conversion_duplicates",
  "Profiles removed as duplicates, as a share of the profiles in the region before step 5, by the kind of group they were in. The label gives the total and, in brackets, the number removed.",
  "Stacked bars per product of the share of profiles removed as duplicates, split within one platform, across platforms, and both."
) : html``
```

```{ojs}
dups = meta ? app.loadAnalysisTable("conversion_duplicates") : null
dupKinds = meta ? app.loadAnalysisTable("conversion_dup_kinds") : null
kindOf = (id, kind, field) => (dupKinds ?? []).filter((r) => r.dataset_id === id && r.kind === kind).reduce((s, r) => s + r[field], 0)
dupRows = (dups ?? []).map((r) => ({
  ...r, key: r.dataset_id,
  within_removed: kindOf(r.dataset_id, "within", "n_removed"),
  across_removed: kindOf(r.dataset_id, "across", "n_removed"),
  both_removed: kindOf(r.dataset_id, "both", "n_removed")
})).map((r) => ({ ...r, removed: r.within_removed + r.across_removed + r.both_removed })).sort(byDataset)
meta ? table(dupRows, [
  { key: "dataset_id", label: "Product", align: "left", format: name },
  { key: "n_profiles", label: "Profiles", title: "Profiles in the region, before step 5" },
  { key: "n_duplicate_profiles", label: "In a group", title: "Profiles sharing their date and position with another, the one kept included" },
  { key: "removed", label: "Removed" },
  { key: "share", label: "Share removed", format: (_, r) => app.formatShare(r.removed, r.n_profiles) },
  { key: "within_removed", label: "Within one platform", title: "Removed from groups on one platform" },
  { key: "across_removed", label: "Across platforms", title: "Removed from groups whose profiles each carry a different platform code" },
  { key: "both_removed", label: "Both", title: "Removed from groups spanning two or more platforms, one of them repeating the cast" },
  { key: "n_platforms_with_duplicates", label: "Platforms with any", format: (v, r) => `${app.formatCount(v)} of ${app.formatCount(r.n_platforms)}` }
]) : html``
```

How large the groups are: the number of groups of each size, from two
profiles up. A group of two is a cast recorded twice; larger ones are the
same cast repeated more often.

```{ojs}
dupSizes = meta ? app.loadAnalysisTable("conversion_dup_sizes") : null
kindOrder = ["within", "across", "both"]
kindName = ({ within: "Within one platform", across: "Across platforms", both: "Both" })
sizeKeys = dupSizes ? [...new Map(dupSizes.map((r) => [r.size, r.size_label]))].sort((a, b) => a[0] - b[0]) : []
sizeRows = dupSizes
  ? app.widen(dupSizes, { index: ["dataset_id", "kind"], column: "size", value: "n_groups", name: (v) => `s${v}` })
      .map((r) => ({ ...r, key: `${r.dataset_id}|${r.kind}` }))
      .sort((a, b) => byDataset(a, b) || kindOrder.indexOf(a.kind) - kindOrder.indexOf(b.kind))
  : []
meta ? table(sizeRows, [
  { key: "dataset_id", label: "Product", align: "left", format: name },
  { key: "kind", label: "Kind", align: "left", format: (v) => kindName[v] ?? v },
  ...sizeKeys.map(([size, label]) => ({ key: `s${size}`, label, title: `Groups of ${label} profiles` }))
]) : html``
```

The platforms behind the groups that span more than one platform (across
platforms, and both): the sets of platform codes that share casts most
often, per product.

```{ojs}
dupSets = meta ? app.loadAnalysisTable("conversion_dup_platforms") : null
viewof setDataset = meta && dupSets
  ? Inputs.select([...new Set(dupSets.map((r) => r.dataset_id))], { label: "Product", format: name })
  : html``
```

```{ojs}
meta && dupSets ? table(
  dupSets.filter((r) => r.dataset_id === setDataset).map((r) => ({ ...r, key: r.platforms })),
  [
    { key: "platforms", label: "Platforms", align: "left", format: (v) => v, wrap: true },
    { key: "n_groups", label: "Groups" },
    { key: "n_profiles", label: "Profiles" },
    { key: "n_removed", label: "Removed" }
  ]
) : html``
```

## Overlap between products

The products of one region come from different streams, and part of what
one holds the other holds too. Two profiles of different products are taken
to be the same cast when they share a date and their positions are within
0.001° of each other in longitude and in latitude (about 100 m or less).
The products rarely store a position to the same last digit, so this is a
tolerance rather than ctddump's rounding to three decimals, which misses a
pair whose two positions fall either side of a rounding boundary. The match
is made twice: with the platform code, and on date and place alone, which
also finds a cast the two products name differently.

```{ojs}
meta ? app.analysisFigure(
  "conversion_overlap",
  "The share of the first product's profiles that the second also has. Dark: matched with the same platform code. Light: matched only on date and place, under a different code.",
  "Stacked bars per pair of products of one region of the share of profiles they share."
) : html``
```

A cast an NRT product shares with CORA has been through CORA's
reprocessing as well, so the share of an NRT product found in CORA is how
much of it has a delayed mode counterpart. A regional and a global NRT
product share no platform code, so only the match on date and place can find
what they have in common. Where it finds little, the two products hold
different casts rather than the same casts under different names.

```{ojs}
overlap = meta ? app.loadAnalysisTable("conversion_overlap") : null
compare = meta ? app.loadAnalysisTable("conversion_compare") : null
ctddumpMatch = (ref, other) => (compare ?? []).find((c) => c.reference_id === ref && c.compared_id === other)?.matched_profiles ?? null
meta ? table((overlap ?? []).map((r) => ({ ...r, key: `${r.dataset_id}|${r.compared_id}`, ctddump: ctddumpMatch(r.dataset_id, r.compared_id) })), [
  { key: "dataset_id", label: "Product", align: "left", format: name },
  { key: "compared_id", label: "Also in", align: "left", format: name },
  { key: "n_profiles", label: "Profiles" },
  { key: "n_matched_same_platform", label: "Same platform code", format: (v, r) => `${app.formatCount(v)} (${app.formatShare(v, r.n_profiles)})` },
  { key: "n_matched_any_platform", label: "On date and place", format: (v, r) => `${app.formatCount(v)} (${app.formatShare(v, r.n_profiles)})` },
  { key: "ctddump", label: "ctddump's match", title: "Profiles ctddump's own comparison matches with the platform code, on positions rounded to three decimals", format: (v) => (v === null ? "" : app.formatCount(v)) }
]) : html``
```

### The same cast in NRT and in CORA

A profile an NRT product shares with CORA, on the same platform, date and
place, is one cast in two versions. It should hold the same observations in
both. Most pairs do; the rest differ in their number of observations, and
how they differ says what happened to the cast between the two.

```{ojs}
matches = meta ? app.loadAnalysisTable("conversion_match") : null
meta ? table((matches ?? []).map((r) => ({ ...r, key: `${r.dataset_id}|${r.compared_id}` })).sort(byDataset), [
  { key: "dataset_id", label: "Product", align: "left", format: name },
  { key: "compared_id", label: "Matched in", align: "left", format: name },
  { key: "n_matched", label: "Pairs" },
  { key: "n_same_obs", label: "Same observations", format: (v, r) => `${app.formatCount(v)} (${app.formatShare(v, r.n_matched)})` },
  { key: "n_more_in_dataset", label: "NRT has more" },
  { key: "n_more_in_compared", label: "CORA has more" },
  { key: "n_within_minute", label: "Times within a minute", title: "Pairs whose two profile times are no more than 60 s apart", format: (v, r) => app.formatShare(v, r.n_matched) }
]) : html``
```

```{ojs}
meta ? app.analysisFigure(
  "conversion_match_difference",
  "Pairs of the same cast whose numbers of observations differ, by how much: observations in the NRT profile minus those in the CORA profile. Pairs with the same number are left out; the table above counts them.",
  "Bar charts per NRT product of mismatched pairs by the difference in observations."
) : html``
```

Where in the profile the two versions differ: in the deepest observation,
the shallowest, both, or neither, in which case the ends agree and the
difference is between them.

```{ojs}
meta ? app.analysisFigure(
  "conversion_match_ends",
  "Mismatched pairs by which end of the profile differs between the two versions, split by the side with more observations. An end differs when its pressures are more than 0.5 dbar apart. The number is the pairs in the row.",
  "Stacked bars per NRT product and side of mismatched pairs by the end that differs."
) : html``
```

Three patterns stand out:

- **One more observation in NRT, at the bottom.** The commonest mismatch:
  the CORA version lacks the deepest observation of the NRT one.
- **Many more in CORA, with the same ends.** Mostly in the Arctic part of
  the global NRT product: hundreds more observations over the same depth
  range, which suggests the NRT version is a thinned copy of the cast and
  CORA holds it at full vertical resolution.
- **A few more in NRT, with the same ends.** Observations missing from
  inside the CORA version, as in much of the Baltic.

The platforms with mismatched pairs, per product:

```{ojs}
matchPlatforms = meta ? app.loadAnalysisTable("conversion_match_platforms") : null
viewof matchDataset = meta && matchPlatforms
  ? Inputs.select([...new Set(matchPlatforms.map((r) => r.dataset_id))], { label: "Product", format: name })
  : html``
```

```{ojs}
meta && matchPlatforms ? table(
  matchPlatforms.filter((r) => r.dataset_id === matchDataset).map((r) => ({ ...r, key: r.platform_code })),
  [
    { key: "platform_code", label: "Platform", align: "left", format: (v) => v },
    { key: "n_matched", label: "Pairs" },
    { key: "n_mismatched", label: "Mismatched" },
    { key: "share", label: "Share", format: (_, r) => app.formatShare(r.n_mismatched, r.n_matched) },
    { key: "n_more_in_dataset", label: "NRT has more" },
    { key: "n_more_in_compared", label: "CORA has more" },
    { key: "median_difference", label: "Median difference", title: "Of the mismatched pairs: observations in NRT minus observations in CORA", format: (v) => (v === null ? "" : (v > 0 ? `+${v}` : `${v}`)) }
  ],
  { sortKey: "n_mismatched", descending: true }
) : html``
```

## Other parameters

What else the source files carry. ctddump reads temperature, salinity and
pressure (and depth, where pressure is missing) and leaves the rest.

```{ojs}
extra = meta ? app.loadAnalysisTable("conversion_extra_parameters") : null
extraRows = extra
  ? [...new Set(extra.map((r) => r.dataset_id))].map((id) => ({
      key: id, dataset_id: id, name: name(id),
      parameters: extra.filter((r) => r.dataset_id === id).map((r) => `${r.parameter} (${r.n_files})`).join(", ")
    })).sort(byDataset)
  : []
meta ? table(extraRows, [
  { key: "name", label: "Product", align: "left", format: (v) => v },
  { key: "parameters", label: "Parameters (files)", align: "left", format: (v) => v, wrap: true }
]) : html``
```
